preamble: Loss of the alveolar implosive: [ɗ] disappears. Gravina (2014) describes Proto-Central Chadic *ɗ as "frequently reduced to /ʔ/ or lost altogether". In Proto-Tera *ɗ was deleted word-finally, and in several languages, among them Mbuko and Mandara, word-initial *ɗ before *ɨ was dropped, sometimes with compensatory reduplication of the next consonant (Mafa ɬaɬaj 'egg') and sometimes without it (Mbuko ɬaj). Debuccalization to [ʔ] is the likely intermediate stage.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Central Chadic to Mbuko and Mandara

examples.note: Gravina (2014: 64), example (65). Merey and Gemzek ɗəɬaʸ keep ɗ, and Mafa ɬaɬaj compensates by reduplication.
